## MEDIUM IMPACT

### Component: `ha-tile-container` (Area Card, Tile Card, Shortcut Card)

**What changed:** A new boolean property `.fixedInfoHeight` has been added to `ha-tile-container` in all three cards (`hui-area-card.ts`, `hui-tile-card.ts`, `hui-shortcut-card.ts`). When `fixedInfoHeight` is `true` (i.e., the card is in a grid layout with a fixed row count), the `ha-tile-info` sub-component inside `ha-tile-container` will have its height constrained — and per the release notes, this was added specifically to *allow the area card name to wrap to two lines in vertical layout*.

**What it affects in ha-lcars:** The ha-lcars theme does not directly target `ha-tile-container`, `ha-tile-info`, or their internals in `card-mod-card-yaml`. However, LCARS button classes (`.button-small`, `.button-lozenge-*`, etc.) applied to tile/area/shortcut cards target the inner structure via:

```css
> ha-card, > #aspect-ratio > ha-card, &:is(ha-card) {
  /* sizing, flex layout, height rules */
}
```

If `fixedInfoHeight` causes `ha-tile-info` inside `ha-tile-container` to shift from a single-line to a two-line layout, the overall rendered height of tile/area/shortcut cards placed in fixed-row grid contexts may increase unexpectedly. LCARS button shape classes that rely on `height: 100%` or absolute/flex positioning of inner children (e.g., `.button-small`'s `> .content > #info { margin-top: -24px; }`) could have text overlap or misalignment when the info section wraps.

**Suggested fix:** Test LCARS-styled tile cards, area cards, and shortcut cards specifically in grid views with fixed row counts (i.e., `grid_options.rows` set to a number). If the info text wrapping causes visual misalignment inside LCARS button shapes, add a targeted rule in `card-mod-card-yaml` to constrain or normalize the info area height:

```css
/* In card-mod-card-yaml, inside existing button-class selectors */
:host(.button-small) > ha-card ha-tile-container ha-tile-info {
  overflow: hidden;
  white-space: nowrap; /* or: height: auto; to let it flow */
}
```

The exact fix depends on desired behavior (clip vs. allow wrap). No fix needed if testing shows LCARS-styled cards are not used in fixed-row grid contexts.

### Component: `hui-shortcut-card` and `hui-tile-card` — New `layout` property

**What changed:** Both `hui-shortcut-card` and `hui-tile-card` now accept a new `@property({ attribute: false }) public layout?: string;` which receives the grid layout context from their parent. This is a new property passed down by the grid renderer.

**What it affects in ha-lcars:** No direct CSS impact, but this confirms these cards now have layout-awareness. If future card-mod injection rules attempt to use container queries or attribute selectors on `hui-tile-card` or `hui-shortcut-card` elements (e.g., `[layout="grid"]`), that attribute is not reflected to the DOM (it is `attribute: false`). Any future LCARS attempt to write `hui-tile-card[layout="grid"]` CSS selectors would silently fail.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed now. If the LCARS theme ever needs to differentiate grid vs. non-grid tile card styling, use container queries (`@container`) rather than element attribute selectors, since `layout` is not exposed as a DOM attribute.

## LOW IMPACT

### Component: `tools-template` Panel — WA Split Panel Adoption

**What changed:** The Tools > Template panel (`tools-template.ts`) now uses `ha-split-panel` (a WebAlloy split panel component). This may introduce a `<ha-split-panel>` element in the template tools shadow DOM.

**What it affects in ha-lcars:** The ha-lcars theme has no card-mod rules targeting `tools-template` or the template panel's internals. This is informational only.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed. If LCARS theming of the template panel is desired in the future, the new split-panel layout would need to be targeted. The component element name would be `ha-split-panel`.

---

### Component: `dialog-device-replaced` — Integration logo display

**What changed:** The replace device dialog now shows the integration logo and name (`dialog-device-replaced.ts`). This may add new visual elements (an `<img>` or `<ha-integration-icon>`) to the dialog's shadow DOM.

**What it affects in ha-lcars:** The ha-lcars `card-mod-dialog-yaml` applies only top-level CSS variable overrides (text color, card background) and font rules. It does not inject into the specific replace-device dialog's shadow DOM. No existing selector is broken.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed. The dialog will inherit the standard LCARS dialog variable overrides. Optionally, a `"dialog-device-replaced $"` card-mod rule could be added if logo contrast/sizing needs adjustment against LCARS backgrounds.
